facts.raw_span: 4-week history of watery diarrhea (20 episodes per day)
vomiting
diffuse abdominal pain aggravated by spicy foods
8-kg weight loss (≈15% of body weight)
brownish macules on the hands and feet
hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
onychodystrophy
mild hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia (total protein 3.52 g/dL [normal 6.6–8.3], albumin 2.09 g/dL [3.5–5.2])
zinc deficiency (51 µg/dL [70–120])
low vitamin B12 (<150 pg/mL [300–900])
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms of watery diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss, along with the presence of Yamada polyps and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum, are consistent with Crohn's disease.

The patient's symptoms of diarrhea, abdominal pain, and weight loss, along with the presence of hypoproteinemia, hypoalbuminemia, zinc deficiency, and low vitamin B12, are consistent with celiac disease.

The patient's symptoms of brownish macules on the hands and feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk, and onychodystrophy, along with the presence of multiple type II and III Yamada polyps and numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum, are consistent with Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
The patient's laboratory results show a zinc deficiency, which is consistent with a diagnosis of zinc deficiency.

rationales.F01: Watery diarrhea is a common symptom of Crohn's disease and Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
rationales.F04: Significant weight loss is a red flag for Crohn's disease and other chronic conditions.
rationales.F07: Onychodystrophy can be associated with Crohn's disease and zinc deficiency.
rationales.F09: Zinc deficiency is a known complication of Crohn's disease and other malabsorptive conditions.
rationales.F11: Yamada polyps are characteristic of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome, but can also be seen in other conditions.
rationales.F12: Numerous polyps throughout the colon and rectum are highly suggestive of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome.
